title: RBI in Chicago and Northwest Indiana: Whiting, Joliet, Lemont
description: Risk-based inspection for Chicago-area refineries and pipeline tank farms: cold-climate damage, Illinois and Indiana rules, and remote API 580/581 studies.
h1: Risk-based inspection for Chicago-area refineries, terminals and pipeline storage
eyebrow: Risk-based inspection in Chicago and Northwest Indiana
intro: Three large refineries anchor the Chicago area: BP's Whiting refinery on the Lake Michigan shore in Indiana, ExxonMobil's refinery near Joliet and CITGO's refinery at Lemont, both in Illinois. Around them sit pipeline terminals, products tank farms and chemical plants, fed by crude trunk lines that end around Whiting and Griffith. This page is for integrity and inspection teams at those sites. It covers the cold-climate damage that a Gulf Coast damage list misses, heavy crude and coker service, the different Illinois and Indiana rules, consequence beside the lake and how Atlantis runs a remote RBI study.

highlights.p: Freeze damage in dead legs, wet insulation from leaking tracing, frost heave under tank pads and low-temperature brittle fracture during cold start-ups are screened explicitly, because a damage list written for the Gulf Coast leaves them out.

Indiana runs its own occupational safety plan and boiler rules; Illinois follows federal OSHA, with the State Fire Marshal and the City of Chicago inspecting boilers and vessels. The register records the governing regime for every item so each interval is checked against the right rule.

The assessment is remote. Where CMLs are unread, insulated lines have no CUI history or tanks lack floor data, Atlantis can send UT, MT, PT and VT technicians to Chicago-area sites and feed the readings into the model.

sections.h: Two refining clusters and the tank farms between them
p: The Calumet Region of Lake County, Indiana, holds BP's Whiting refinery, reported at 435,000 barrels a day in 2024 and the largest refinery in the Midwest, with its crude units, cokers, hydrotreaters, tank fields and docks on the lake shore. Terminals in Whiting, East Chicago and Hammond receive and ship products by pipeline, truck, rail and lake vessel, and crude trunk lines from Canada and the western states terminate around the Whiting and Griffith area. Integrated steelworks fill much of the rest of the shoreline.

South-west of Chicago, ExxonMobil's refinery near Joliet in Will County, reported at 251,800 barrels a day, and CITGO's Lemont refinery, reported at about 184,000, sit within a short drive of petrochemical and polymer plants around Channahon and Morris, with products terminals, pipelines and barge docks along the Des Plaines and Illinois rivers tying them together. Chicago's south side adds liquid terminals around Lake Calumet and the Calumet River. The result is a region where an RBI programme may need to cover a very large refinery, a cluster of pipeline tankage and several mid-sized terminals, each under a different mix of rules.

sections.h: Cold-climate damage a Gulf Coast template misses
p: Most published RBI examples come from warm, humid refining centres, and a damage list carried over from one of them will treat winter as an afterthought. In northern Illinois and north-west Indiana, cold drives several mechanisms directly. Hard freezes split dead legs, drains and instrument connections where water has collected; steam and electric tracing that leaks or fails wets insulation and starts corrosion underneath; freeze-thaw cycling opens jacketing seams and keeps insulation damp well into spring; and lake-effect humidity off Lake Michigan adds to the moisture load on the shoreline.
The assessment screens for each of these item by item, using the data that governs them rather than a blanket assumption.
list: Dead legs, low points, drains and small-bore connections: freeze risk depends on whether water can collect, whether the line is traced and how it is drained during an outage
Steam-traced and heat-traced lines: tracing leaks are a common source of wet insulation, so tracing maintenance records are an input to the CUI screen
Insulated carbon steel in or cycling through the susceptible temperature range, with jacketing condition and insulation age recorded
Brittle fracture during cold start-up, depressurisation or hydrotest in winter, screened from material toughness, minimum design metal temperature and operating history
Tank pads and foundations: frost heave and settlement, checked against survey data where it exists
Floating and fixed roofs: snow and ice loads, frozen roof drains and seals stiffened by cold

sections.h: Heavy crude, cokers and the refinery risk picture
p: With crude trunk lines from western Canada ending in the region, much of the crude available to Chicago-area refineries is heavy and high in sulfur, and Whiting operates cokers to convert the bottom of the barrel. For an RBI model that brings a familiar set of mechanisms with some regional emphasis. High-temperature sulfidation in crude, vacuum and coker units depends on sulfur, temperature and, for carbon steel, silicon content; naphthenic acid corrosion follows the acid number of the crude and the velocity in hot sections; and heavy crude's solids and salts put pressure on desalters, so overhead chloride corrosion is a standing concern.

Coke drums are a class of their own. They cycle between hot filling and quenching on cycles measured in hours, and their damage is thermal fatigue, bulging and cracking at the shell, the skirt attachment and circumferential welds rather than steady thinning. An RBI plan names those components separately, assigns inspection that can find cracks and distortion, and records each drum's cycle history; evaluating a bulged or cracked drum for continued service is engineering work for the owner, not part of the risk assessment. Hydroprocessing effluent systems and hydrogen service equipment are screened for ammonium bisulfide corrosion and high temperature hydrogen attack against API RP 941.

sections.h: Pipeline terminals and products tanks around Lake County and Chicago
p: The tank farms around Griffith and Hammond and along the Chicago-area pipeline corridors are dominated by large crude tanks, many of them external floating-roof designs, operated by pipeline companies, alongside products terminals with mid-sized internal floating-roof gasoline tanks, distillate tanks and ethanol and additive storage. Products terminals carry more gasoline in summer and more distillate in winter, so service changes are part of the normal year and a tank's product history matters to its damage assessment.

Tanks that relieve surges or hold crude for reinjection into a hazardous liquid pipeline are breakout tanks, and under the current federal rule their internal intervals stay on measured floor corrosion rates; the risk ranking still directs coverage, prove-up and sequencing among them. Terminal tanks outside the pipeline system can use API 653's risk-based internal interval within its conditions, subject to any state requirement. In Indiana, IDEM's aboveground tank registration and release-reporting requirements add another reason to record each tank's location and consequence carefully. Out-of-service floor work is usually planned from spring to autumn to avoid lake-effect winters.

sections.h: Illinois, Indiana and Chicago: who regulates what
p: Whiting and its neighbours sit in Indiana; Joliet, Lemont and the Chicago terminals sit in Illinois. The state line changes several of the regimes an RBI plan answers to, and the City of Chicago adds its own inspection programme within city limits. The register records the governing body for each item, so the inspector can see at a glance which intervals the risk assessment can set freely and which need confirming elsewhere.

sections.h: Consequence beside Lake Michigan and dense neighbourhoods
p: The probability side of an RBI assessment asks how likely an item is to fail; the consequence side asks what happens if it does, and on the Chicago lakefront that answer is unusually heavy. Whiting's refinery sits on the shore of Lake Michigan, a drinking water source for millions of people, and close to residential streets. A release that reaches the lake, a storm sewer or groundwater carries an environmental consequence far larger than the same release on an inland site with clay soils and no nearby water.

The study therefore treats consequence inputs as engineering data rather than defaults: inventory groups and isolation valve locations, detection and isolation times, drainage paths and the distance to surface water, soil and groundwater conditions under tank fields, and the population around the fence line. Getting those inputs right changes the ranking. An item with modest probability can rise to the top of the plan because of where a leak would go, and the inspection effort follows.

sections.h: Storms, power loss and forced shutdowns
p: Severe summer storms reach the region as well as winter cold. On July 15, 2024, storms cut power to the Joliet refinery and forced it to shut down, with multiple units taken offline. Unplanned shutdowns and restarts are hard on equipment: thermal transients stress welds and flanged joints, water condenses in lines that are normally hot and dry, and some damage mechanisms, such as polythionic acid stress corrosion cracking in sensitised stainless steel, are associated with shutdown conditions rather than normal operation.

An RBI plan for a Chicago-area site names an unplanned shutdown, a major storm and an extended winter outage as reassessment triggers, each with a short list of checks for the items most exposed. The list typically covers stainless equipment susceptible to shutdown cracking where protective procedures were not followed, insulated lines that sat cold and wet, traced lines whose tracing failed during the outage, and tank roofs and drains after heavy rain or snow.

sections.h: Turnaround timing in a short outdoor season
p: Turnarounds at a refinery the size of Whiting add thousands of inspection items and draw contractors from across the Midwest, and outdoor inspection is slower and riskier in winter, when cold affects couplant behaviour, coating cure, battery life and footing on roofs and stairways. The useful outdoor season for tank floors and much external work runs roughly from spring to autumn.

The plan helps in two ways. It marks every task as needing the unit shut down, suitable for on-stream completion before the outage, or deferrable to a later window, and it places on-stream thickness surveys, corrosion mapping and external inspections in the warmer months wherever the due dates allow. After each turnaround the findings come back into the model: corrosion rates are updated, inspection effectiveness is credited for the methods and coverage actually achieved, and the next plan starts from measured condition.

sections.h: How the remote study runs, and who approves it
p: The data room for a Chicago-area study holds the usual engineering record, from P&IDs, PFDs and heat and material balances to datasheets, data reports and CML thickness history, plus process chemistry and crude assay summaries, integrity operating windows, tracing and insulation records for cold-climate screening, coke drum cycle histories where relevant, and for tanks the full inspection file with foundation and settlement data. Video workshops with your process, operations, corrosion and inspection people run in Central time, the same as Houston, and the Hyderabad side of the team keeps working through the data between them. Probability and consequence can be evaluated with a qualitative matrix, a semi-quantitative method, the quantitative approach of API RP 581 or the RBI standard your company already uses.

When the records leave a gap, your own inspectors normally collect the data, and Atlantis can also send UT, MT, PT and VT technicians to Chicago-area and Lake County sites for baseline thickness surveys, corrosion mapping after insulation removal and surface examination of welds where cracking is credible. Radiography is not an Atlantis service anywhere in the United States, so radiographic work stays with your licensed contractor. Approval rests with your inspection organisation: the API 510, 570 or 653 inspector, a state- or city-commissioned inspector for jurisdictional equipment, or the operator's inspection authority. Atlantis does not act as inspector of record, and fitness-for-service assessments of damage found in service remain with your engineer rather than with Atlantis.

faqs.q: Which cold-weather damage mechanisms should be in a Chicago-area RBI study?
faqs.a: At minimum, freeze damage in dead legs, drains and small-bore connections, corrosion under insulation wetted by tracing leaks and freeze-thaw cycling, brittle fracture during cold start-ups or winter hydrotests, frost heave and settlement under tank pads, and snow, ice and drain problems on tank roofs. Each is screened item by item from the data that governs it.

faqs.q: Does the Whiting area answer to federal OSHA or Indiana OSHA?
faqs.a: Indiana runs its own occupational safety plan, so process safety management for private employers in Indiana is enforced by IOSHA, which applies standards at least as effective as the federal rule. Illinois private employers fall under federal OSHA. The RBI evidence an inspector expects is much the same on both sides of the state line, but the register records the enforcing agency.

faqs.q: Do Illinois or Indiana regulate pressure vessel inspection intervals?
faqs.a: Both have boiler and pressure vessel programmes: the State Fire Marshal's Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety in Illinois, with the City of Chicago inspecting inside city limits, and the Department of Homeland Security's Boilers and Pressure Vessels Section in Indiana. Jurisdictional items are listed separately so their accepted intervals can be confirmed before a risk-based plan changes them.

faqs.q: How do coke drums fit into an RBI programme?
faqs.a: As a separate class with their own mechanisms. Drums cycle hot and cold many times a year, so their damage is thermal fatigue, bulging and cracking at the shell, skirt attachment and circumferential welds rather than steady thinning. The plan names those components, assigns crack-capable inspection and records cycle history; judging whether a damaged drum can stay in service is your engineer's call.

faqs.q: Are the pipeline tanks around Griffith and Hammond breakout tanks?
faqs.a: Many will be, if they relieve surges or store crude for reinjection into a hazardous liquid pipeline, and their internal intervals then stay on measured corrosion rates under the current federal rule. Terminal tanks outside the pipeline system may use API 653's risk-based option. The study classifies each tank with your compliance staff before the plan is written.

faqs.q: How should an unplanned shutdown or power loss feed into the plan?
faqs.a: As a reassessment trigger with a short check list. Typical checks cover stainless equipment susceptible to polythionic acid cracking where shutdown protection was not applied, insulated lines that sat cold and wet, traced lines whose tracing failed and tank roofs after heavy rain or snow. Clean findings are recorded and the intervals stand; damage brings the affected items forward.

faqs.q: Can Atlantis technicians work at Whiting, Joliet or Lemont?
faqs.a: Yes. Atlantis can send UT, MT, PT and VT technicians to Chicago-area and Lake County sites for baseline thickness readings, corrosion mapping once insulation is removed and surface examination of welds in cracking service. They work under the refinery's own safety and permit system, and radiographic work remains with your licensed contractor.

Your inspector of record, whether the API 510, 570 or 653 inspector, a commissioned inspector for jurisdictional equipment or the operator's inspection authority. The study recommends intervals and shows their basis but does not approve them. If damage turns up that needs an engineering judgement on continued service, your engineer makes it and the model is updated afterwards.
